findings: The complete guide covers ordering, a cancelable Pending state lasting at least 30 minutes, Ready to ship with cancellation closed, and Shipped when tracking is available. It also identifies Canceled, Delivered and Undeliverable.

The optional Hardware Orders API preview step validates and estimates taxes without creation. Country-matched available SKUs and shipping methods must share a provider; account manager, monthly invoice billing and sales eligibility assessment apply to preview access.

Dashboard returns require eligible shipped or delivered Dashboard orders in supported countries and user permission. The package must include original packaging and accessories within 30 days, the first initiated return refunds shipping fees, and receipt at the distribution facility triggers the refund, with credit card funds taking up to 10 days.
substantive_changes: The November guide adds order-time preregistration of eligible smart readers. One selected Terminal location per order can be changed on the details page until serial numbers are available. Stripe then automatically registers eligible readers. For multiple locations, wait for serial numbers and register readers individually by serial number.

For accounts with Hardware Orders API preview access, Stripe can emit registered or registration_failed per-device outcomes following automatic attempts. The event data.object is a Hardware Order Device, which can be correlated by device ID, serial number and hardware order relationship. These are additions alongside six order-level events.
The documented Stripe-Version header changes from 2026-04-22.dahlia to 2026-10-28.endive while terminal_hardware_orders_beta stays v5, including the webhook endpoint version guidance.

The 2026-11-07 self-service list has 32 entries versus 33 in May. GI is no longer listed for self-service but remains in the distinct shipping table. Both captures direct merchants outside self-service to Support from the Dashboard order.
historical_claims_to_preserve: Keep the full 2026-05-01 capture, six order-state webhooks and earlier version pairing as dated evidence. Keep historical v3/v4 same-mode duplicate shipped-event warning and v3/v4 status mapping without generalizing to v5.

Preserve Dashboard permissions, cutoff and signature thresholds by shipping destination, shipping/returns distinction, 30-day fallback guidance, and sandbox-only status helpers. The cap is 10,000 of each item in a single order in both captures.
Keep existing manual registration methods as separate routes from November order-time automation, and preserve the original packaging, accessories and first-return shipping-fee qualifications.
conflicts: The mapped source, company page and Terminal hardware concepts retain an undated 33-country return count or GI listing. The Stripe index's 33-country locator is already labeled 2026-05-01 (wiki/stripe-index.md:194) and should remain historical while its retrieval wording is refreshed for the November 32-entry list. GI remains in the shipping table.

The mapped source and wiki/concepts/stripe-terminal-hardware-orders.md:59-70 retain the May header and order-only event inventory as the undated picture. Date the earlier pairing and six order events, and add November's preview-dependent device events.

The mapped source and both Terminal hardware concepts say 10,000 units per order; each capture says up to 10,000 of each item in a single order. The mapped introduction at wiki/sources/source-stripe-terminal-order-and-return-readers.md:13 and dedicated concept imply API returns. The captures document API creation and retrieval, with eligible Dashboard self-service returns and a Dashboard-to-Support route when unavailable.

The mapped raw link implies 37 destinations in the shipping table. Both tables have 40 destination rows; remove or correct the count. The broad fleet concept's ship-to-any-location wording needs the documented destination and physical-address qualifications.

The related concept at wiki/concepts/stripe-terminal-hardware-orders.md:15 calls the API preview public. The November guide documents preview access through a sales eligibility assessment, a Stripe Account manager, agreement to monthly invoice billing, and acknowledgment of timely preview updates (new raw lines 212-220). Scope the concept to these qualified accounts.
unresolved_questions: The 2026-11-07 capture omits GI from the self-service list but does not give the operational effective date or account-specific eligibility. The capture does not enumerate all preregistration-eligible smart-reader models.

findings: Add the dated November order-time preregistration, location/serial boundaries, beta header and distinct device outcomes, and update the dated self-service return scope while retaining the prior raw.

answers.Q1: For https://docs.stripe.com/terminal/fleet/order-and-return-readers, the captures document Dashboard purchase of pre-certified hardware and accessories and up to 10,000 of each item in a single order (old raw line 20 and new raw line 21). Pending orders are cancelable in the Dashboard and remain pending at least 30 minutes. Ready to ship ends cancellation, tracking advances the order to Shipped, and the November retained v4 diagram shows Pending also branching to Canceled and Shipped branching to Delivered or Undeliverable (old raw lines 26-39 and new raw lines 27-48). The Hardware Orders API is preview for sales-assessed eligible accounts, with a Stripe Account manager and agreement to monthly invoice billing (old raw lines 194-216 and new raw lines 212-234). API order creation uses matching country- and provider-compatible SKUs and shipping methods, with the country filter required, optional validation and tax estimation without creation, then order creation and retrieval (old raw line 222 and old raw lines 238-264 and old raw lines 286-292 and old raw lines 317-333, new raw line 240 and new raw lines 256-282 and new raw lines 304-310 and new raw lines 335-351). November adds selecting one editable Terminal location per order until serial numbers appear. Stripe then automatically registers eligible smart readers, with individual serial registration for orders split across locations and preview-access-dependent per-device outcomes (old raw lines 39-45 and old raw lines 335-344, new raw lines 50-58 and new raw lines 353-364). Eligible self-service returns are documented in Dashboard for Dashboard orders placed and shipped within the listed-country scope, with appropriate permissions and Shipped or Delivered status. For devices outside self-service, the Dashboard order's Contact support action sends details to Support. The 30-day original-packaging and accessories qualifications apply, receipt triggers the refund, and shipping fees are refunded for the first initiated return (old raw lines 41-49 and old raw lines 87-101 and old raw lines 122-124, new raw lines 60-68 and new raw lines 105-119 and new raw lines 140-142). November's self-service list has 32 entries and omits GI, versus 33 in May (old raw lines 51-85 and new raw lines 70-103). The current source-stripe-terminal-order-and-return-readers covers the historic lifecycle but omits preregistration and still uses the May header, six-event and return-country details. Its line 13 implies an API return route, which the captures do not establish, and it overgeneralizes the per-item cap.
answers.Q2: For https://docs.stripe.com/terminal/fleet/order-and-return-readers, update source-stripe-terminal-order-and-return-readers. The latter concern automatic attempts on eligible devices and use the Hardware Order Device payload, rather than an order-wide outcome (old raw line 216 and old raw lines 335-344, new raw lines 50-58 and new raw line 234 and new raw lines 353-364). The inline diagram is newly retained state-transition representation, with no evidence of a lifecycle change (old raw lines 26-39 and new raw lines 27-48). Preserve the reciprocal stripe-terminal-hardware-orders route, its parent stripe-terminal fleet route and the Stripe company and index source routes. Date their old return and header claims and keep manual registration discoverable through source-stripe-terminal-register-readers. Correct the mapped summary's line 13 and dedicated concept to distinguish the documented API creation/retrieval from eligible Dashboard self-service for Dashboard orders placed and shipped within listed countries with proper permissions, and Dashboard-to-Support when self-service is unavailable (old raw lines 41-49 and old raw lines 122-124 and old raw lines 290-311 and old raw lines 317-333, new raw lines 60-68 and new raw lines 140-142 and new raw lines 308-329 and new raw lines 335-351). Correct the order limit to 10,000 per item per order (old raw line 20 and new raw line 21).
